attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you click on the melody parameter in the [play melody] block, then select a tile in each column?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓Did you test out different melodies to add to your game, using the Editor?

❓How does the sound change as you tinker with the melody parameter?

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to tinker with the melody in the Editor. Encourage them to notice the different notes played when they click different boxes within the same column, and across different rows. If they want, the ninja can also explore the Gallery to select preset melodies.


💡Point out to the ninja that the higher the number used as the tempo parameter, the faster the melody will play.
steps.instructions:
Add some music to make this project more exciting! Open the Music code block menu then drag out a [play melody] block into the [on start] container.


Click on the melody parameter to open the Editor. Click one box in each column to create a melody for the project. Click ▶ to test the melody before clicking Done to add it to the project. 


Change the tempo parameter to play the melody faster or slower. 


Click ▶ to listen to the music playing in the project!

steps.hints: ❓  Did you change the playback mode in the [play melody] block so that the melody repeats over and over?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


﻿Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when you change the playback mode parameter of the [play melody] block?

❓What does changing the parameter of the [set volume] block do to the melody?

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡There are 3 different playback modes available for all [play] blocks in the Music category: until done, in background, and looping in background. “Until done” plays the music or sound one time through and then continues on to the next block in the code. “In background” plays the music or sound one time, but does not wait until it is done to continue on to the next block in the code. “Looping in background” plays the music or sound repeatedly, and continues on to the next block in the code immediately after the music or sound starts.
steps.instructions:
Make the music play on a loop and change the volume! 


Click ⏷in [play melody] block to change the playback mode to [looping in background]. 


Open the Music code block menu then drag out a [set volume] block above the [play melody] block. Tinker with the volume parameter to adjust how loudly the music plays.


Click ▶ to listen to the music play over and over again, at a different volume, in the project!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you place a new [play melody] block in an [if true then] conditional that checks if life is equal to 1?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens to the music when the Player sprite has more than one life? What happens to the music when the Player sprite has only one life left?

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the ninja to notice that the [if true then] conditional container block will only run if the statement is true. Prompt the ninja to think about what condition needs to be met, in order for the different melodies to be played.

💡Point out to the ninja that the higher the number used as the tempo parameter, the faster the melody will play.
steps.instructions:
Change the melody when the Player has only 1 life left!


Open the Logic code block menu and drag an [if true then] conditional into the bottom of the [on sprite overlaps sprite] block. 


Open the Logic code block menu and drag out a [0=0] value block to replace <true>. Open the Info code block menu and drag out a life value block into the first white bubble of the [0=0] block. In the second bubble of the [0=0] value block, set the number to 1. 


Open the Music code block menu and drag another [play melody] block into the [if true then] conditional. Create a new melody that plays at a faster tempo. Click ⏷to change the playback mode to [looping in background]. 


Click ▶ to hear the new melody play when the Player has only 1 life left!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add a [stop all sounds] block to both the [if true then] conditional and the [on life zero] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does a [stop all sounds] block need to be used in the code?

❓ Where should the [stop all sounds] blocks be placed so the correct music or sound is stopped?

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Remind the ninja that the [stop all sounds] block will need to come before the block that creates the new music or sound, otherwise that new music or sound will also be stopped! This is also true for “built in” sound effects, like the sound effect that plays for the [game over] block.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The 2 melodies are playing at the same time when the Player sprite has 1 life left!


Open the Music code block menu and drag a [stop all sounds] block above the [play melody] block inside the [if true then] conditional. 


Then, drag another [stop all sounds] block above the [game over] block inside the [on life zero] container block.


Click ▶ to hear each melody play at the correct time, and stop when the game over sound effect plays.

sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Projectile, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    info.changeLifeBy(-1)
    otherSprite.destroy()
})
info.onLifeZero(function () {
    game.gameOver(false)
})

scene.setBackgroundColor(13)
let mySprite = sprites.create(img`

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses music and conditionals to enhance the game experience!

validationItems.text: 2 different melodies are looping in the background of the project.
The volume of the melody is changed.
The melodies are stopped before another melody or sound effect is played.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Yellow Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about using animation and music to make your projects even more awesome! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: The Ol’ Razzle Dazzle
badges.description: Use animation and music to enhance a project.

badges.title: Saturday Morning Cartoons
badges.description: Use both image and movement animation in a project.

badges.title: On and On and On and...
badges.description: Repeat a melody or sound on loop in the background of a project.

badges.title: Original Score
badges.description: Compose a custom melody in MakeCode.
